I am 69 years old, been farming these 2 mu for 50 years. Small plot, just me and my wife, one of the children works in town. Let me think about this year like I always do — I do what worked last year, maybe adjust a little.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed from the town shop — the one most neighbors in my village buy, "Jimai" type. Two mu is small, I buy about 30 jin of seed. Before planting I put down the base fertilizer — one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's 50 jin, the 15-15-15 kind. Then at returning-green in spring I topdress urea, about 30 jin per mu. That's my habit. My neighbor old Wang uses a bit less and his yield is fine, but I am scared to cut it — if the wheat is yellow I lose more money than I save. Better put a little extra.

I water the wheat at planting, then at returning-green, then at jointing, then at filling. Four times from the well. The well is ours, electricity is the main cost. I spray for aphids and the wheat head disease once or twice — depends what I see. Plough with the small tractor before planting, I pay the machine man.

For maize in summer, I plant right after wheat harvest, no tillage, just drill the seed in. Hybrid seed — Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has, everyone buys the same. I put compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 40 jin per mu, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, 40 jin per mu. Maize eats a lot. I water once or twice if no rain in July-August. Spray once for borers.

I don't weigh potash separately — it's in the compound fertilizer. I never bought straight potash. Phosphorus same — from the compound.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 jin per mu, maize about 550 jin per mu. I expect the same.
